gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has big, round counters that read like open parentheses. Conthrax keeps every stroke one width and geometric, which lets those rounded, glassy counters below it do the softening.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings crayon-tall strokes and terminals cut back to leave a big gap. And Conthrax, which has no calligraphic modulation, can take the larger size while the body stays modest.

gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Conthrax never mixes bold and light strokes inside a word, so each line looks geometric and cut clean. Noto Sans Hebrew then carries the reading, its big midsection and wide curve gaps keeping paragraphs easy going.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-hk: Wide, tall-bodied and clean-cut, Conthrax draws contrast-free strokes from stem to terminal. Noto Sans HK reads smoothly beneath it, with large lowercase and brush ends lifted away before each curve closes.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads friendly and open, its c ends pointing apart like pincers. Conthrax is best at crisp, uniform-stroke display lines, while the body font is best at steady text.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Conthrax has no hairlines to squint at, just wide geometric letters whose lowercase rises nearly to the capitals. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian adds big open eyes and a deep middle band.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-noto-sans-jp: Conthrax builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, giving display text a precise, geometric look. Noto Sans JP, a sans-serif with a very tall x-height, can stay modest in size.
